text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Coffee is inching higher and looks to be getting ready for a test of resistance, technical analysts said.
Traders called benchmark September to open $20-25 higher.

"It's heading for a big test at $1,750," said Darren Gurner, technical analyst at Sucden. But he noted resistance before then, particularly at the gap between $1,720 and $1,735. "I think we'll see the market at least test up to these levels," he said.

New York coffee futures ended sharply higher on Tuesday as technically driven local and speculative buying propelled the September contract past $2 per lb for the first time in eight weeks, traders said.
Guatemala exported 129,559 60-kg bags of coffee in July, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said on Tuesday.
Exports for the month were 32 percent lower than July 1996 exports of 189,673 60-kg bags, Anacafe president Julio Arrivillaga said in a statement.
Colombia's main coffee harvest could begin one month late because of heavy rains during the flowering period earlier this year, a coffee expert said on Tuesday.

"Our registers show the flowering period was about one month late. We think, therefore, that the harvest can be expected to be about one month late," Orlando Guzman, an agroclimatologist at the CENICAFE research center, said.

Indonesian coffee supplies are very tight with several exporters hanging on to their beans in the hope of seeing higher prices, while a sharp fall in output is aggravating the situation, traders said on Wednesday.
No damaging cold is in sight for Brazil's coffee growing areas in the next 5 days, forecaster Weather Services Corp said.
